answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring capital commitment to validate network transitions. An attacker must acquire a majority of total stake, forcing costs to a prohibitive glacier of expenditure. While market volatility may push token value toward a nadir, the barrier remains high. Much like a singular opal embedded in secure hardware, each staked unit serves as a verifiable anchor, ensuring that identity proliferation cannot bypass the economic cost of consensus participation.
